heard: Good morning, and welcome back. This is a 25-minute strength session with a kettlebell and a pair of dumbbells, and I'll be with you the whole way.
Here's the plan. A short warm-up, three rounds of strength work, one finisher, and an easy cooldown to bring the heart rate home.
One rule, before we start. Move only as far as feels easy on that left knee today. If anything feels sharp, stop and take the easier version I'll give you.
Let's begin the warmup. 30 seconds of marching in place. Lift the knees, swing the arms, and start now.
Stand tall. Shoulders down and away from the ears. Breathe through the nose and let the arms swing loose.
3, 2, 1, and switch.
Hip circles now. Hands on the hips. Big slow circles to the right for 20 seconds.
Other way.
First strength move, the goblet squat. Hold the kettlebell close to your chest, elbows pointing down, feet a little wider than your hips.
Set your feet, set your feet. Escape the chest proud and stand up, but driving the floor away. Two seconds down, one second up.
Three sets of ten, with 45 seconds of rest between sets. Set 1 starts now.
Go.
If the heels lift, widen the stance a little and sit back. You should feel this in your quadriceps and your glutes, not your lower back.
Blast rep. Stand all the way up, squeeze and rest.

While you rest, a quick one. On this day in 1781, the British Army surrendered at Yorktown, and the story goes that a band played a tune called The World Turned Upside Down. Historians still argue about whether it really happened.
15 seconds left in the rest. Pick up the dumbbells. 5, 4, 3, 2, 1.
Romanian deadlift. Dumbbells in front of your thighs, a soft bend in the knees, and push your hips straight back like you're closing a car door with your backside.
Feel the stretch in your hamstrings, keep the back flat, and stop when the weights pass your knees. Then drive the hips forward and stand tall.
If you have the 25 pound dumbbells, use those. If 10 reps feel easy, add two more next time, and write it down.
Begin.
Halfway there. Keep the weights close to your legs the whole way down.
That's it. Strong and steady. You've done harder things than this before breakfast, four more.
Hold.
Quiz time while you rest. Which planet has the longest day in our solar system? It's Venus. One day there lasts longer than its whole year, about 243 Earth days.
Round two of three. Same weights, same tempo. Get set and go when you're ready.
How hard was that, out of 10? If it was a 7 or an 8, you picked the right weight. If it was a 9, take the lighter pair for the last round.
Next, the Paloff press. Standing side onto the band, press your hands straight out from your chest and don't let the band pull you around.
10 presses with the band on your left side. Then we switch to the right side.
3, 2, 1, switch sides.
Bulgarian split squat. Right foot forward, left foot back on the bench, lower straight down until the back knee hovers just above the floor.
Keep it shallow on the left side today. Half the depth is fine. The goal is smooth, pain-free reps, not a personal record.
Here comes the finisher. 40 seconds of kettlebell swings, 20 seconds of rest, 3 rounds. Hips snap, arms float, breathe out hard at the top.
Last round. Everything you've got left. Snap those hips. 10 seconds. Finish strong.
Stop. Park the bell.

Fun fact while your breathing settles. The kettlebell started life in Russian markets in the 1700s as a counterweight for weighing grain. Farmers began swinging them at fares to show off their strength.
Walk it out for 30 seconds. Easy steps around the room, shake out the hands, and let the heart rate come down on its own.

One more thing to think about. Researchers at McMaster University found that short bursts of hard effort, just a few minutes a week, improved fitness markers in sedentary adults, small doses add up, which is why today counts.
Cooldown. Stand easy and breathe in slowly through your nose for four counts.
Hold it gently at the top.
and let it out even slower through your mouth for six counts. That the shoulders drop.
Step your left foot back into a gentle calf stretch. Press the heel into the floor and hold for 20 seconds. No bouncing.
Today you did 30 gobbit squats, 30 Romanian deadlifts, 40 pal oaf presses, and about 60 kettlebell swings. That's 2,000 pounds moved give or take.
That was good work today. You showed up, you kept the knee happy, and you finished strong. Drink some water, and I'll see you on Thursday.
You are done. Nicely done.
